## Review Lecture 2
### Michaelis-Menten kinetics

$$E + S \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} ES \xrightarrow{k_2} E + P$$

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{S}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = -k_1[\mathrm{E}][\mathrm{S}] + k_{-1}[\mathrm{ES}]$$

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{E}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = -k_1[\mathrm{E}][\mathrm{S}] + (k_{-1} + k_2)[\mathrm{ES}]$$

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{ES}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = k_1[\mathrm{E}][\mathrm{S}] - (k_{-1} + k_2)[\mathrm{ES}]$$

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathrm{P}}{\mathrm{d}t} = k_2[\mathrm{ES}] \equiv v$$

---

$$\mathrm{E}_o = [\mathrm{E}] + [\mathrm{ES}]$$

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{S}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = -k_1 \mathrm{E}_o [\mathrm{S}] + (k_1 [\mathrm{S}] + k_{-1})[\mathrm{ES}]$$

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{ES}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = k_1 \mathrm{E}_o [\mathrm{S}] - (k_1 [\mathrm{S}] + k_{-1} + k_2)[\mathrm{ES}]$$

Initial conditions:

$$[\mathrm{S}]_{t=0} = \mathrm{S}_o$$
$$[\mathrm{E}]_{t=0} = \mathrm{E}_o$$
$$[\mathrm{ES}]_{t=0} = 0$$
$$[\mathrm{P}]_{t=0} = 0$$

## Review Lecture 2
### Equilibrium binding and cooperativity

$$\mathrm{S} + \mathrm{P}_{j-1} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{P}_j$$

Adair's Equation:

$$r = \frac{\mathrm{K}_1 [\mathrm{S}] + 2\mathrm{K}_1 \mathrm{K}_2 [\mathrm{S}]^2 + 3\mathrm{K}_1 \mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{K}_3 [\mathrm{S}]^3 + \dots + n\mathrm{K}_1 \mathrm{K}_2 \dots \mathrm{K}_n [\mathrm{S}]^n}{1 + \mathrm{K}_1 [\mathrm{S}] + \mathrm{K}_1 \mathrm{K}_2 [\mathrm{S}]^2 + \dots + \mathrm{K}_1 \mathrm{K}_2 \dots \mathrm{K}_n [\mathrm{S}]^n}$$

$$\mathrm{K}_j = \frac{[\mathrm{P}_j]}{[\mathrm{P}_{j-1}][\mathrm{S}]} \quad \begin{array}{l} \text{macroscopic association constant} \\ \text{for transitions between state } j-1 \text{ and } j \end{array}$$

---

## Note #1 Detailed balance

$$\mathrm{P}_o \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_{+1}}{\rightleftharpoons}} \mathrm{P}_1 \underset{k_{-2}}{\overset{k_{+2}}{\rightleftharpoons}} \mathrm{P}_2 \quad \dots \quad \mathrm{P}_{n-1} \underset{k_{-n}}{\overset{k_{+n}}{\rightleftharpoons}} \mathrm{P}_n$$

$$0 = \frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{P}_o]}{\mathrm{d}t} = -k_{+1}[\mathrm{P}_o][\mathrm{S}] + k_{-1}[\mathrm{P}_1]$$

$$\begin{aligned}
0 = \frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{P}_1]}{\mathrm{d}t} &= -k_{+2}[\mathrm{P}_1][\mathrm{S}] + k_{-2}[\mathrm{P}_2] + k_{+1}[\mathrm{P}_o][\mathrm{S}] - k_{-1}[\mathrm{P}_1] = \\
&= -k_{+2}[\mathrm{P}_1][\mathrm{S}] + k_{-2}[\mathrm{P}_2]
\end{aligned}$$

$$\text{etc.} \quad \longrightarrow \mathrm{K}_j \equiv \frac{k_{+j}}{k_{-j}} = \frac{[\mathrm{P}_j]}{[\mathrm{P}_{j-1}][\mathrm{S}]}$$

---

## I Identical and independent binding sites

<!-- Diagram of two identical independent binding sites transitioning from empty, to singly bound (top and bottom states), to doubly bound -->

$$\mathrm{K} = k_+ / k_- \qquad \mathrm{K}_1 = 2\mathrm{K} \qquad \mathrm{K}_2 = \mathrm{K} / 2$$

$$\text{use Adair:} \quad r = \frac{2\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}] + 2\mathrm{K}^2[\mathrm{S}]^2}{1 + 2\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}] + \mathrm{K}^2[\mathrm{S}]^2} = \frac{2\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}]}{1 + \mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}]}$$

---

## II Non-identical and independent binding sites

<!-- Diagram of non-identical independent binding sites with rate constants k+, k- and k+*, k-* -->

$$\mathrm{K} = k_+ / k_-$$
$$\mathrm{K}^* = k_+^* / k_-^*$$

$$\text{Independent binding:} \quad r = \frac{\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}]}{1 + \mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}]} + \frac{\mathrm{K}^*[\mathrm{S}]}{1 + \mathrm{K}^*[\mathrm{S}]}$$

---

## III Identical and interacting binding sites

<!-- Diagram of identical interacting binding sites with intrinsic and cooperative transition rates -->

$$\mathrm{K} = k_+ / k_- \qquad \mathrm{K}_1 = 2\mathrm{K} \qquad \mathrm{K}_2 = \mathrm{K}^* / 2$$
$$\mathrm{K}^* = k_+^* / k_-^*$$

$$\text{use Adair:} \quad r = \frac{2\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}] + 2\mathrm{K}\mathrm{K}^*[\mathrm{S}]^2}{1 + 2\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}] + \mathrm{K}\mathrm{K}^*[\mathrm{S}]^2}$$

---

## Cooperativity

$$r = \frac{2\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}] + 2\mathrm{K}\mathrm{K}^*[\mathrm{S}]^2}{1 + 2\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}] + \mathrm{K}\mathrm{K}^*[\mathrm{S}]^2}$$

$$\mathrm{Y} = \frac{x(1 + \beta x)}{1 + 2x + \beta x^2} \qquad \begin{aligned} \beta &= \mathrm{K}^* / \mathrm{K} \\ x &= \mathrm{K}[\mathrm{S}] \end{aligned}$$

$\beta > 1$: positive cooperativity  
$\beta > 2$: sigmoidal curve  
$\beta < 1$: negative cooperativity  
(always: $\mathrm{d}^2\mathrm{Y}/\mathrm{d}x^2 < 0$)

## The lysis-lysogeny decision:

<!-- Diagrams showing phage injection and decision between lysis and lysogeny -->

As the phage genome is injected phage genes are transcribed and translated by using the host’s machinery.

Which set of phage proteins are expressed determines the fate of the phage: lysis or lysogeny

Image by MIT OCW.

---

Image removed due to copyright considerations.

A lysogen is immune to invasion of another phage. Repressor dimers turn off genes in the injected phage chromosome. High concentration of repressor keeps cell in lysogenic state.

---

## The lysis-lysogeny decision is a genetic switch

<!-- Diagram of the lambda phage genetic switch showing cI, cI transcript, O_R (O_R3, O_R2, 17 bp, O_R1), cro, cro transcript, P_RM, P_R, and RNAp -->

only ‘space’ for one RNA polymerase (mutual exclusion)

Image by MIT OCW. After Ptashne, Mark. *A genetic switch : phage lambda.* 3rd ed. Cold Spring Harbor, N.Y. : Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press, 2004.

---

Single repressor dimer bound - three cases:

I **Negative control**, dimer binding to OR2 **inhibits** RNAp binding to right $\mathrm{P_R}$ promoter.

**Positive control**, dimer binding to OR2 **enhances** RNAp binding to left $\mathrm{P_{RM}}$ promoter.

Image removed due to copyright considerations.  
See Ptashne, Mark. *A genetic switch: phage lambda.*  
3rd ed. Cold Spring Harbor, N.Y.: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press, 2004.

---

II **Negative control**, dimer binding to OR1 **inhibits** RNAp binding to right $\mathrm{P_R}$ promoter.

**Negative control**, dimer binding to OR1 **inhibits** RNAp binding to left $\mathrm{P_{RM}}$ promoter (too distant).

Image removed due to copyright considerations.  
See Ptashne, Mark. *A genetic switch: phage lambda.*  
3rd ed. Cold Spring Harbor, N.Y.: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press, 2004.

---

III **Negative control**, dimer binding to OR3 **inhibits** RNAp binding to left $\mathrm{P_{RM}}$ promoter.

**Positive control**, dimer binding to OR3 **allows** RNAp binding to right $\mathrm{P_R}$ promoter.
